contexts.title: Bridge Alert Management
contexts.summary: Manufacturer-defined (unlisted) alerts under IEC 62923-2 with identifiers 10000–9999999.

symptoms.title: Alert ID in 10000–9999999 range
symptoms.detail: CAM or ECDIS shows an alert whose identifier is outside the Annex A standard list.

symptoms.title: Alert presents with poor or missing text
symptoms.detail: Priority/category shows, but the human-readable description is blank, generic, or untranslated.

symptoms.title: Repeated unlisted alert from one equipment
symptoms.detail: Same manufacturer ID reappears after acknowledge/silence from radar, INS, AIS, or other BAM source.

symptoms.title: Responsibility transfer fails for the alert
symptoms.detail: Alert cannot be transferred or remains orphaned on CAM after source equipment reset.

contexts.title: Engine-room AMS / UMS
contexts.summary: Alarm points that appear on the AMS/HMI but are missing from the ship’s approved alarm list, IOM, or set-point schedule.

symptoms.title: Active alarm not on approved alarm list
symptoms.detail: Tag/point number shows on the AMS but has no matching entry in the class-approved alarm list.

symptoms.title: Unknown tag or channel after retrofit
symptoms.detail: New or renamed I/O after yard work, upgrade, or spare-channel enablement.

symptoms.title: Group of unexplained alarms in one zone
symptoms.detail: Several undocumented or unexpected alarms from the same cabinet, loop, or 24 V branch.

symptoms.title: Heard on extension but unclear on panel
symptoms.detail: Duty cabin / bridge extension annunciates, but panel text is blank, truncated, or generic.

bam-unknown-id.title: Capture the alert identity
actions: Record alert identifier, priority, category, source equipment, time, and CAM state (active / acknowledged / silenced).
Photograph or export the ALF / alert log entry if available.
Note own-ship operating mode (harbour, sea, autopilot, INS modes).
checks: Identifier is numeric and in 10000–9999999 (manufacturer-defined / unlisted).
Source equipment name matches the physical unit raising the condition.

bam-unknown-id.title: Match against manufacturer documentation
actions: Open the source equipment alert list (maker’s BAM / alert identifier list required by IEC 62923-2).
Search by identifier first, then by displayed text.
Confirm the assigned meaning, recommended bridge response, and whether the alert is safety-related.
checks: Maker list includes this ID.
Documented meaning matches the observed operating condition.
bam-unknown-id.ifMissing: Treat as incomplete manufacturer documentation. Escalate to maker/service and keep the alert active in the investigation log—do not ignore it because it is unlisted.

bam-unknown-id.title: Verify the physical condition
actions: Inspect the reported function on the source equipment (sensor feed, COM loss, power, antenna, heading source, etc.).
Compare with redundant sensors / backup equipment where fitted.
Check recent configuration changes, software updates, and interface cabling.
checks: A real equipment or interface fault explains the alert.
No concurrent earth fault or power anomaly on navigation equipment supplies.

bam-unknown-id.title: Contain and document
actions: Apply the maker’s recommended bridge procedure; use backup navigation methods if the function is impaired.
Log the ID, meaning, root cause, and corrective action in the bridge alert / defect book.
Update the vessel’s local BAM quick-reference with this unlisted ID so the next watch recognises it.
checks: Alert clears only after the cause is fixed—not by silencing alone.
Local quick-reference and defect report are updated.

bam-no-text.title: Preserve evidence before reset
actions: Record identifier, source, priority, and any partial text.
Export CAM / equipment logs if the HMI allows.
Do not power-cycle the source solely to clear an unread message until evidence is captured.
checks: Identifier alone is enough to look up the maker list.

bam-no-text.title: Resolve text from the maker list
actions: Look up the identifier in the equipment’s BAM alert catalogue.
Check language pack / HMI text database integrity if other alerts also lack text.
Compare software version with the version tied to the alert catalogue on board.
checks: Catalogue entry exists for the ID.
HMI language and software version are consistent with the catalogue.

bam-no-text.title: Restore presentation and close out
actions: Correct language/database faults per maker guidance, or arrange service reload.
Add the ID and plain-language meaning to the bridge quick-reference.
Retest by inducing a safe, maker-approved test alert if available.
checks: Future activations show usable text on CAM and source equipment.

bam-repeat.title: Separate nuisance from standing fault
actions: Count activations per watch and note whether acknowledge clears presentation only.
Check whether the underlying condition remains true on the source equipment.
Review cluster behaviour—related standard alerts may explain the unlisted one.
checks: Standing fault vs intermittent interface noise is identified.

bam-repeat.title: Trace interface and power
actions: Inspect serial/Ethernet/NMEA links used by the source equipment.
Check 24 V / UPS feeds, earthing, and recent cable work near the unit.
Swap to redundant link or backup sensor if the architecture allows.
checks: Communication errors, CRC faults, or power dips correlate with the alert.

bam-repeat.title: Correct cause; never ‘normalise’ by silence
actions: Repair the interface/sensor/power fault.
If maker guidance allows a temporary inhibit, record it with owner, reason, and restoration time.
Update the unlisted-ID quick-reference with the proven cause pattern.
checks: Alert stays clear through a full watch after repair.
Any inhibit has a restoration plan.

bam-transfer.title: Confirm BAM role and category
actions: Verify which station owns the alert (source, CAM, BNWAS-related roles as fitted).
Confirm alert category/priority still allow transfer under current operating mode.
Check time sync between CAM and source equipment.
checks: Category and operating mode explain transfer limits, or they do not.

bam-transfer.title: Recover communications
actions: Inspect BAM network / IEC 61162 links between source and CAM.
Review recent configuration of alert reporting (ON/OFF per alert).
Restart only after logging state, following maker recovery order.
checks: ALF / reporting path is healthy.
Other alerts from the same source still transfer correctly.

bam-transfer.title: Close the orphaned alert safely
actions: Resolve or acknowledge at the source per maker procedure.
Confirm CAM presentation matches source state after recovery.
Log the failure mode for service—unlisted alerts with broken transfer are a documentation and safety risk.
checks: No orphaned active state remains on CAM.

ams-not-on-list.title: Freeze the identity of the point
actions: Record AMS tag/point number, display text, group, priority, time, and value/status at activation.
Export or print the alarm history line.
Note whether the point is analog, digital, calculated, or serial-imported.
checks: You can uniquely identify the point even if the ship alarm list omits it.

ams-not-on-list.title: Search every on-board definition source
actions: Check approved alarm list, set-point schedule, I/O list, cable schedule, and maker IOM.
Search AMS engineering/configuration pages for the tag (may be enabled but never exported to the paper list).
Ask whether yard or service enabled a spare channel recently.
checks: Configuration database contains the point even if the printed list does not.
Or the point is truly undefined—treat as configuration fault.

ams-not-on-list.title: Prove process vs signal fault
actions: Read the live value at the AMS and compare with a local gauge / tester at the sensor.
Check loop power, cable continuity, shielding, and earth faults on the 24 V panel.
If digital, verify the field contact state independently of the AMS card.
checks: Field condition matches AMS, or the signal chain is false.

ams-not-on-list.title: Restore documentation and protection
actions: Correct the root cause (process or signal).
Update the approved alarm list / set-point schedule and configuration backup.
Function-test sensor → AMS → extension → bridge/cabin as applicable. Record measured trip value.
checks: Point is documented, tested, and not left inhibited without a register entry.

ams-orphan-tag.title: Identify retrofit lineage
actions: Compare current I/O map with the last yard/service red-line drawings.
List recent PLC/AMS downloads, HMI theme updates, and spare-channel enables.
Interview the last technician who modified the cabinet or software.
checks: Change window that introduced the tag is known.

ams-orphan-tag.title: Decide: legitimate new point or leftover
actions: If the field device is real and required, commission it fully (set point, text, priority, extensions, alarm list).
If leftover/test point, disable or remove per maker procedure and back up the clean configuration.
Never leave an undocumented active point in UMS.
checks: Every enabled point has text, set points, and list coverage—or is deliberately removed.

ams-orphan-tag.title: Regression test the affected group
actions: Lamp/audible test the panel.
Re-test neighbouring points on the same card or network node.
File configuration backup location and checksum/version in the technical file.
checks: No collateral points were disabled or renumbered incorrectly.

ams-false-cluster.title: Classify local vs general engine-room fault
actions: Map alarms to cabinets, loops, and 24 V branches.
Check earth-fault indication and supply voltage/ripple on the AMS distribution.
Note whether one maker’s serial package is flooding the AMS with bad imports.
checks: Pattern points to power/earth, one I/O rack, or one serial source.

ams-false-cluster.title: Isolate safely while keeping watch
actions: Increase manning / cancel UMS if machinery protection is compromised.
For positive earth suspects, isolate branch fuses in turn only when safe and logged.
For negative earth suspects, lift instrument earths methodically with labels—only under active watchkeeping.
checks: Critical parameters have an alternate monitoring plan while isolating.

ams-false-cluster.title: Repair, then re-prove the group
actions: Repair cable/insulation, PSU/batteries, or serial gateway as found.
Clear standing alarms only after field verification.
Update drawings if spare channels or temporary links were involved.
checks: Cluster does not return across a heat/load cycle.
UMS is resumed only after extension and dead-man tests pass.

ams-extension-only.title: Correlate extension with panel state
actions: At the moment of the extension call, read the AMS first-up / history.
Check duty selection, cabin volume, and isolation switches.
Confirm whether a generic ‘engineers call’ masks a specific unlisted point.
checks: The extension event is tied to a concrete AMS point ID.

ams-extension-only.title: Repair presentation path
actions: Fix blank/truncated text in the HMI database for that point.
Verify group acknowledgement logic is not hiding the first-up identity.
Test extension to duty cabin, public spaces, and bridge.
checks: Panel text and extension behaviour identify the same point.

ams-extension-only.title: Document for the next UMS period
actions: Add the point to the alarm list if missing.
Brief the next duty engineer on the new text/ID.
Record the extension test in the UMS checklist file.
checks: UMS checklist shows a successful extension test after the fix.

safetyRules: An unlisted alarm is still an alarm—silence is not a repair.
Do not permanently inhibit or widen a set point without a written cause, owner, and restoration time.
If machinery protection or bridge situational awareness is in doubt, increase manning and cancel UMS / use backup navigation methods.
Capture identifier, source, time, and operating context before resetting equipment.
Update the alarm list, BAM quick-reference, and configuration backup whenever a point is confirmed.
